class.name: Captain (LotR)
class.proficiency: Constitution, Charisma, Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Persuasion, Survival
class.armor: Light Armor, Medium Armor, Heavy Armor, Shields

trait.name: Captain
trait.text:
He stood up, and seemed suddenly to grow taller. In his eyes gleamed a light, keen and commanding.
When the world is on the brink of ruin, it is the duty of all individuals of worth to rise and take the lead, whatever the risk. You have chosen to put your judgement to the service of others, to guide them in this dark hour. But you don't want others to heed your commands out of fear or obedience — you want them to follow you because they trust you.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 45

feature.name: Starting Captain
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Captain, you begin play with 10 + your Constitution modifier hit points.
You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.
• Armor: light armor, medium armor, heavy armor, shields • Weapons: simple weapons, martial weapons • Tools: none • Skills: Choose 2 from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Persuasion, and Travel
You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment provided by your background.
• (a) ring mail or (b) hide armor • (a) a martial melee weapon and a shield or (b) a martial melee weapon and a simple melee weapon • (a) a bow and a quiver of 20 arrows or (b) two simple melee weapons
If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 5d4 × 10 gp to buy your equipment.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 45

feature.name: Multiclass Captain
feature.text:
If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose captain as one of your classes.
Ability Score Minimum: As a multiclass character, you must have at least 1 of the following ability score(s) to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a captain.
• Strength 13 • and Charisma 13
Proficiencies Gained: When you gain your first level in a class other than your initial class, you gain only some of your new class's starting proficiencies, here are the proficiencies you gain when you take your first level as a captain.
• Armor: light armor, medium armor, heavy armor, shields • Weapons: simple weapons, martial weapons • Tools: none
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 67

feature.name: Shadow Path
feature.text:
Lure of Power: When individuals are given a position of authority, either by rank, lineage, or stature, they may end up mistaking their own aggrandizement for the greater good of the people they should be guiding or keeping safe. Power is the quintessential temptation, and provides the Shadow with an easy way to win the hearts of those who desire it.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Leadership
feature.text:
You possess the ability to direct others to action — when under pressure, other people naturally turn to you for guidance. As an action in combat, choose a number of friendly creatures (which can include yourself within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you, up to twice your proficiency bonus. Each creature can gain temporary hit points equal to your Captain level + your Charisma modifier. These temporary hit points last until they are depleted or the creature finishes a short or long rest. You must then finish a short or long rest to use this feature again.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Fighting Style
feature.text:
At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your speciality. Choose one of the following options. You cannot take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Fighting Style: Defense
feature.text:
While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Fighting Style: Dueling
feature.text:
When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Fighting Style: Great Weapon Fighting
feature.text:
When you roll damage for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can treat any roll of 4 or less on a damage die as a 5. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Fighting Style: Protection
feature.text:
When a creature you can see hits you or a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to the target's AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss. You must be wielding a shield or a finesse weapon.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Virtue
feature.text:
At 2nd level, and again at 4th, 6th, 8th, and 10th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice (see Chapter 4). You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 2nd, 6th, and 10th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list (see page 64).
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Captain Title
feature.text:
There are many titles that Captains can acquire during their career, the most common of which are the Chieftain and the Thane.
At 3rd level, you receive a title as a reward for your accomplishments. Choose Chieftain or Thane, both detailed at the end of the calling description. The title you choose grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th level.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Valiant
feature.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any saving throw you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
At 4th level, you can take an additional common or cultural virtue of your choice (see Chapter 4). You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.text:
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
At 6th level, you can take an additional common or cultural virtue of your choice (see Chapter 4). You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 6th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list (see page 64).
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Aura of Valour
feature.text:
Starting at 6th level, whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you hit a target with a melee weapon attack, the creature can add your Charisma modifier to the damage roll. You cannot grant this bonus if you are frightened or unconscious.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
At 8th level, you can take an additional common or cultural virtue of your choice (see Chapter 4). You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
At 10th level, you can take an additional common or cultural virtue of your choice (see Chapter 4). You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 10th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list (see page 64).
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Aura of Courage
feature.text:
At 10th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you cannot be frightened while you are conscious (but can still accumulate Shadow points from Dread).
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Captain Title: Chieftain
feature.text:
As a chieftain you are both a leader and a weaponmaster, accustomed to leading your comrades by jumping first into battle.
"Here is Aragorn son of Arathorn, chieftain of the Dúnedain of Arnor, Captain of the Host of the West..."
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 46

feature.name: Challenge (Chieftain)
feature.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you can issue a challenge to a creature you can see within 10 feet of you as a bonus action. You gain advantage on melee attack rolls against the creature for 1 minute or until it drops to 0 hit points or falls unconscious. In addition, the creature must make a Wisdom (Insight) check (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). On a failed check, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you for the duration, until you attack another creature, if a creature friendly to you attacks the target, or if you end your turn more than 30 feet away from the target. You must then finish a short or long rest to use this feature again.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 47

feature.name: Pursuer of Foes (Chieftain)
feature.text:
Starting at 7th level, creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the Disengage action. In addition, when you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 47

feature.name: Captain Title: Thane
feature.text:
You have sworn service to a King and serve as one of their chosen fighters. As long as war must be, you stand ready to protect the innocent and destroy your lord's enemies.
From dark Dunharrow in the dim morning/with thane and captain rode Thengel's son:/to Edoras he came, the ancient halls/of the Mark-wardens mist-enshrouded...
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 47

feature.name: Bright Blade (Thane)
feature.text:
Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can imbue a melee weapon that you are holding with your bravery. For 1 minute, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls made with that weapon (with a minimum bonus of +1). For the duration of the effect, when you hit a creature, the next attack roll against the target made by an attacker other than you has advantage if the attack is made before the start of your next turn. If you are no longer holding or carrying this weapon, or if you fall unconscious, this effect ends. You must then finish a short or long rest to use this feature again.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 47

feature.name: Tireless Leader (Thane)
feature.text:
Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you suffer the effects of exhaustion as if it was one level lower (no effects at level 1, disadvantage on ability checks at level 2, and so on).
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 47
